sentences.text: In respect of an accident which is not in dispute, which resulted in the death of Gangashamaiah, a 62 year old, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.8,13,400/- as compensation.
2. The owner of the offending vehicle as well as the claimants are in appeal.

3. The Tribunal on assessment of the evidence adduced before it has come to the conclusion that Gangashamaiah, who was driving the motor-cycle bearing registration No.KA-02/EK-7146 was hit by a lorry bearing registration No.KA-01/AG-9666 on 13.08.2014.
4. The owner of the lorry however contends that his vehicle was never involved in the accident.

It is contended that the lorry was seized by the Police on 05.09.2014 and a complaint was lodged by the owner to the Magistrate regarding illegal seizure and a show cause notice was also issued to the Inspector and immediately thereafter, a Mahazar was prepared indicating that the vehicle was seized and on 15.10.2014, the lorry in question was also released.
It is therefore contended that the lorry owned by the appellant-owner was never involved in the accident.

5. The learned counsel for the claimants who have filed the appeal seeking enhancement of compensation contend that the involvement of the lorry cannot be in dispute since the Police after thorough investigation have laid a charge-sheet against the person who was driving the lorry.

6. He also contends that the IMV report which has been produced as Ex.P-9 clearly indicates that there is damage to the bumper of the lorry and this by itself indicates that there was involvement of the lorry in the accident.
7. The entire argument of the owner is that his vehicle was not involved in the accident which occurred on 13.08.2014.

In order to establish this contention, primarily, the owner of the lorry had to establish that his lorry was either not being used on 13.08.2014 or had been utilized at a place other than the place of the accident.

However, no evidence has been adduced either by the owner or by the driver of the said lorry to the effect that the vehicle was not in use or was in use at a place other than the place of the accident.
8.

It has to be noticed here that a lorry is a commercial asset and it would have to be necessarily put Sri Mahesh B K vs Smt Mangalamma on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111657746/
5 to use every day in order to recover the investment made on it.

sentences.text:
If the contention of the driver who was examined is to be accepted that he was working for five years as a driver, it would also automatically follow that there must be some record indicating that the lorry was put to use, such as a logbook or any other record, which is maintained indicating the manner in which the vehicle was being used.
9.
Unfortunately, no such evidence was produced to indicate that the lorry in question was either not in use on that day or it was being used in a place other than the place of the accident.
Viewed in this background, the IMV report which was produced as Ex.P-9 assumes significance.

Since the IMV report indicates that there was a damage to the right end bumper of the lorry and the son of the deceased has also deposed before the Tribunal stating that he saw the accident and the lorry in question caused the accident, it will have to be held that the lorry was involved in the accident.

No doubt, he has stated that due to the manner in which the accident occurred, he was unable to note down the registration number of the lorry and immediately thereafter inquiries were made and the lorry was detected.
This is a plausible explanation given the fact that the son was seeing his father hit by a vehicle.

10. In my view, it may also be pertinent to state here that the Police after investigation have actually laid a charge-sheet only against the person who was driving the lorry in question and the charge-sheet also indicates that the driver of the lorry did not possess a driving licence and therefore, there was a breach of the policy conditions.

11. In my view, having regard to the charge sheet and more importantly, the IMV report, it will have to be held that the lorry in question was involved in the accident which resulted in the death of Gangashamaiah.
The findings of the Tribunal as regards the involvement of the lorry cannot therefore be found fault with.

12. The argument that the owner of the lorry had lodged a complaint to the Police about the illegal seizure on 05.09.2014 would really be of no relevance since the - 10 - location of the lorry as on the date of the accident would be relevant and not the subsequent seizure.
13. In this view of the matter, I find no merit in the appeal by the owner of the lorry that his vehicle was not involved in the accident in question and the same is accordingly dismissed.

14. As far as the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.8,13,400/- as compensation under the following heads:
Compensation Sl.

1. Loss of estate 15,000/-

sentences.text: In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income of the - 11 - deceased notionally at Rs.17,700/- and after deducting 50% of the same (Rs.8,850/-) towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, as he was a bachelor, it has proceeded to award a sum of Rs.7,43,400/- towards loss of dependency.

16. In my view, though the deceased had left behind his wife, five children and mother, since he was aged 62 years as on the date of the accident, it would be appropriate to deduct 1/3rd (i.e.,
Rs.5,900/-) from the monthly income of Rs.17,700/- that the deceased was drawing as a pension.
Consequently, the net monthly income of the deceased would be Rs.11,800/-.
17. As the deceased was above 60 years, future prospects cannot be added.

18. As the deceased was aged 62 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport - 12 - Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121, a multiplier of '7' would have to be applied.

19. Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.9,91,200/- (Rs.11,800/- x 12 x '7')
towards "loss of dependency".
20.

The claimants being the wife, five children and a mother of the deceased, each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.3,08,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

21. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :

sentences.text: Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.13,32,200/- as against Rs.8,13,400/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
23. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.

24. Since the charge sheet indicates that the driver of the lorry did not have a license, this would be a case of there being a breach of policy conditions and consequently, the principle of pay and recovery will have to be applied.

25. The Insurance Company is therefore directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded along with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and thereafter proceed to recover the same from the owner of the lorry in question, since the charge-sheet had been laid against the - 14 - driver of the lorry and that he did not possess the driving licence.
26. The amount deposited by the owner shall be made over to the Tribunal for disbursement to the claimants and the balance amount shall be paid by the insurer.
27. The appeal by the claimants is accordingly allowed in part and the appeal by the owner is dismissed.
